newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan LCD makers eye new demand, to boost output.
newsitem.headline: Japan LCD makers eye new demand, to boost output.

text.p: Japanese makers of liquid crystal displays (LCDs) said on Monday they plan to boost production as they expect the market to grow following recent robust sales of personal computers (PCs).

Analysts said the domestic market for LCDs is expected to reach 1.23 trillion yen ($10.0 billion) in 1997/98, up from 985 billion yen ($8.07 billion) expected for the current fiscal year ending on March 31.
"Companies are rushing to build new production lines so that they can supply LCDs which are cost competitive," said Yoshiharu Izumi, an analyst at UBS Securities Ltd.
Japan supplies 90 percent of the world's LCDs.

Fujitsu Ltd said on Monday it is considering building a second plant to make thin-film transistor (TFT) LCDs somewhere in Japan by early 1999. Investment in the plant is likely to reach 100 billion yen ($819 million), it said.
"We are considering such an investment because of rapidly growing demand for LCDs," a Fujitsu spokeswoman said, adding that sales of notebook PCs continue to be strong.
"Flat-panel LCDs should also start being used in desk-top personal computers, adding to new demand," she said.
Fujitsu hopes to sell 150 billion yen ($1.22 billion) worth of LCDs in 2000/01, about 7.5 times the sales expected in 1996/97. It currently makes 100,000 LCD sheets per month.
Sharp Corp the world's top LCD maker, also said on Monday that it is considering building a new TFT-LCD plant at its Mie factory in western Japan.
A spokesman for the company, however, said he could not confirm a Japanese newspaper report that total investment in the project may reach 60 billion yen ($491 million).

Sharp said in January that it plans 49 billion yen ($401 million) worth of investment in LCD production facilities in 1997/98, up from 38 billion yen ($311 million) expected in the current business year ending on March 31.
The company currently makes 390,000 sheets per month.
Toshiba Corp said it plans to invest more than 10 billion yen ($81.9 million) to start mass production of a new type of TFT-LCD as early as this autumn.
The new LCD is made with low-temperature polysilicon instead of amorphous silicon, and processes image data more quickly than amorphous silicon LCDs, a company spokeswoman said.
Toshiba also said it plans to boost production at its joint venture plant with International Business Machines Corp by 50 percent to 300,000 sheets a month by early 1998.
Analysts said the boost in production, while temporarily eroding prices, will eventually broaden the market for LCDs by making it cost-effective to use them in a wider range of products.

"The LCD prices will likely decline momentarily at the beginning of the next business year due to the deterioration of the demand-and-supply condition, but the decline in prices will further expand the market," UBS's Izumi said. ($1=122 yen)
